chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) issued a ruling in Yemen regarding a people whose house collapsed upon them, and two boys remained: one free and the other a slave. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) cast lots between them, and the lot fell on one of them; he gave him the wealth and freed the other.
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided between a free person and a slave when both survive a disaster?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, illustrates the application of *qur'ah* (casting lots) as a decisive legal mechanism in inheritance disputes where two heirs of different statuses—free and slave—survive a single event. It highlights the Imam’s pragmatic approach to resolving conflicting claims by assigning the estate to one and manumission to the other, thereby balancing material inheritance with spiritual liberation. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in handling ambiguous survivorship scenarios through equitable distribution rather than rigid proportional division.
